claims.claim: Flex's CPI/Axiom path links AI compute demand to a physical power-and-thermal bottleneck: higher rack density requires power conversion, grid stabilization, backup power, cooling and scalable manufacturing; Flex's 800 VDC rack and proposed EPC Power acquisition extend its exposure from manufacturing into system-level power conversion.

EPC Power's reported 15+ GW deployed base and planned U.S. capacity above 30 GW in 2027 provide evidence of existing infrastructure relevance, but the $4.4 billion acquisition has not yet closed and its projected 2027 growth/margin profile remains an expectation rather than realized economics.

The planned Axiom separation can sharpen causal exposure to AI/grid infrastructure, but it also changes the entity boundary: post-spin Flex and Axiom will have different bottlenecks and demand profiles, so current FLEX structural conclusions must not be mechanically carried across the separation.

risks.risk: Power-conversion technology can be substituted by competing architectures/vendors; scale and integration, not exclusivity, are the defensible mechanism visible today.
Separation changes which public entity owns the CPI bottleneck exposure.

unknowns.unknown: EPC Power standalone customer concentration and realized post-close economics are not yet demonstrated.

claims.claim: The EPC Power transaction creates a concrete financing risk: Flex disclosed a $4.4 billion purchase value and expects debt/equity funding, while the spin proxy describes a committed bridge facility up to $4.4 billion and anticipates SpinCo/Axiom indebtedness or other financing to repay it.

Acquisition and separation are concurrent execution loads. The spin remains conditional on board, shareholder, Singapore High Court, Form 10 effectiveness and other approvals; therefore expected strategic focus is not yet an observed outcome.
Projected EPC Power 2027 revenue growth and ~30% EBITDA margin are management expectations, not current realized evidence; treating them as present economics would inflate confidence.

risks.risk: Up to $4.4 billion bridge financing and post-spin refinancing can increase leverage/financing sensitivity before acquisition synergies are realized.
Management attention, systems, controls, customer/supplier relationships and capital structures face simultaneous acquisition/separation complexity.

unknowns.unknown: Final permanent financing mix, post-spin credit profile and realized EPC Power margins remain unresolved future outcomes.
